title: Cap. VI Arg. 5: from election's inseparable help — certainty of causality, not bare science
latin: Quinto, ab adjutorio inseparabili electionis sive praedestinationis probamus illam non ex fide nostra sed ex mero Dei beneplacito pendere. Nam electio importat certitudinem salutis quoad hominem electum, eamque non nudae scientiae (nam sic Deo ab omni aeternitate certissima sunt, quae sunt maxime fortuita) sed causalitatis, praedestinatione ita operante, ut certo perducat praedestinatum ad vitam aeternam.
pass_a: Fifthly, from the inseparable help of election or predestination we prove that it hangs not from our faith but from the mere good pleasure of God. For election imports a certainty of salvation as regards the elect man, and that not of bare science (for so to God from all eternity those things are most certain which are most fortuitous) but of causality, predestination so operating that it certainly leads the predestined to eternal life.
pass_b: Fifth argument: from election's inseparable help — it hangs not on our faith but on God's mere good pleasure. Election means certainty of salvation for the elect person: not bare knowledge (even the most chance events are utterly certain to God from eternity) but causality — predestination so working that it surely leads the predestined to eternal life.

lemmas.gloss: certainty of causality, not bare science

title: Cap. VI Arg. 5: Matt. 24; Rom. 11:5; Eph. 1:11 — elect salvation certain because God so acts
latin: Unde illud Matth. xxiv. Adeo ut seducant, si fieri posset, etiam electos. Et Rom. xi. 5. Reservatio secundum electionem. Et Ephes. i. 11. Cum essemus praedestinati secundum propositum ejus qui omnia efficit ex consilio voluntatis suae. Quoad Deum igitur certa est salus electorum; quia ex decreto electionis statuit miris modis ita agere in cordibus eorum ut perducantur ad fidem et paenitentiam, ut in fide et vitae novitate permaneant, ac tandem moriantur in Domino.
pass_a: Whence that of Matt. 24: So as to deceive, if it were possible, even the elect. And Rom. 11:5: A remnant according to election. And Eph. 1:11: Being predestinated according to the purpose of him who works all things after the counsel of his will. As regards God therefore the salvation of the elect is certain; because from the decree of election he has determined so to act in their hearts by wonderful ways that they may be led to faith and penitence, that they may remain in faith and newness of life, and at last die in the Lord.
pass_b: Hence Matt. 24 (to deceive, if possible, even the elect), Rom. 11:5 (a remnant according to election), and Eph. 1:11 (predestined according to the purpose of him who works all things by the counsel of his will). Quoad God, the elect's salvation is certain: from the election decree he has resolved so to work in their hearts that they are led to faith and penitence, remain in faith and newness of life, and at last die in the Lord.

lemmas.lemma: Matth. xxiv / Rom. xi. 5 / Ephes. i. 11
lemmas.gloss: elect cannot finally be deceived; remnant; purpose
from election decree God so acts in hearts

title: Cap. VI Arg. 5: Arminian foresight — certainty only from God intuiting, not specially causing
latin: At in illa Praedestinatione Arminiana, ubi fides praevisa post se trahit electionem, nulla est certitudo salutis ex Deo specialiter causante, sed solummodo ex Deo intuente. Nam in quatuor Arminii decretis, quibus praedestinationis naturam describit, nullum est quod certitudinem salutis singulari alicui personae apportet, per modum causae infallibiliter operantis; sed salutem electorum Deo certam relinquit per modum intuentis.
pass_a: But in that Arminian Predestination, where foresighted faith draws election after itself, there is no certainty of salvation from God specially causing, but only from God intuiting. For in the four decrees of Arminius, by which he describes the nature of predestination, there is none that brings certainty of salvation to any singular person, by way of a cause infallibly operating; but he leaves the salvation of the elect certain to God by way of one intuiting.
pass_b: In Arminian predestination, where foresighted faith drags election after it, there is no certainty of salvation from God as special cause — only from God as onlooker. Of Arminius's four decrees describing predestination, none gives any singular person certainty of salvation by an infallibly operating cause; elect salvation stays certain to God only as one who sees.

lemmas.gloss: by way of one intuiting / looking on

title: Cap. VI Arg. 5: Arminius's four decrees — Mediator, believers, means, foresight of users
latin: Primo, ponit decretum de dando Mediatore. Secundo, adjungit aliud, de salvandis credentibus et perseverantibus propter hunc Mediatorem. Tertio, de administrandis mediis ad fidem necessariis. Quarto, de salvandis illis quos praevidet beneficio horum mediorum crediturus et perseveraturos. In tribus prioribus manifestum est nullam certitudinem salutis singulari personae causari; quia communia sunt, et aeque ad reprobos atque electos spectare possunt, quoad nudam decretorum formam.
pass_a: First, he sets down a decree of giving a Mediator. Second, he adds another, of saving believers and those who persevere on account of this Mediator. Third, of administering the means necessary to faith. Fourth, of saving those whom he foresees will believe and persevere by the benefit of these means. In the three prior it is manifest that no certainty of salvation is caused for a singular person; because they are common, and can equally regard reprobates and elect, as far as the bare form of the decrees.
pass_b: First: a decree to give a Mediator. Second: to save believers and perseverers for that Mediator's sake. Third: to administer the means needed for faith. Fourth: to save those he foresees will believe and persevere by those means. The first three cause no certainty of salvation for any one person — they are common, and in bare form can as well cover reprobates as elect.

title: Cap. VI Arg. 5 close: fourth decree only intuits — so election from good pleasure, not foresight faith
latin: Quartum vero decretum, quod solum de singularibus personis agit, certitudinem salutis non affert per modum causae operantis, sed per modum scientiae praevidentis: quia Deus ibi non statuit fidem et perseverantiam in electis efficaciter producere, sed eosdem tanquam jam credituros et perseveraturos intueri. Ubi igitur nulla est certitudo salutis ex Deo specialiter et infallibiliter causante, ibi non est vera illa electio Scripturis celebrata. Ergo electio pendet ex mero Dei beneplacito, non ex fide praevisa.
pass_a: But the fourth decree, which alone deals with singular persons, does not bring certainty of salvation by way of an operating cause, but by way of foreseeing science: because God there does not determine efficaciously to produce faith and perseverance in the elect, but to intuit the same as already about to believe and persevere. Where therefore there is no certainty of salvation from God specially and infallibly causing, there is not that true election celebrated in the Scriptures. Therefore election hangs from the mere good pleasure of God, not from foresighted faith.
pass_b: The fourth decree alone touches singular persons — and even it gives certainty only as foreseeing knowledge, not as an operating cause: God does not there resolve to produce faith and perseverance in the elect, but only to regard them as already about to believe and persevere. Where salvation is not certain from God specially and infallibly causing, there is not the election Scripture celebrates. So election hangs on mere good pleasure, not foresighted faith.

lemmas.gloss: by way of foreseeing science only
